agency_full: National Aeronautics and Space Administration / Jet Propulsion Laboratory / Southwest Research Institute (principal investigator)
payload: Polar Jupiter orbiter; first solar-powered spacecraft to operate beyond the asteroid belt (~50 m² triple-junction solar arrays delivering ~14 kW at Earth, ~500 W at Jupiter)
credit: © NASA / JPL-Caltech / Southwest Research Institute — U.S. Government work, public domain. Juno is the first spacecraft to enter a polar orbit around Jupiter, allowing it to map the planet's magnetic field, gravity field, and atmospheric chemistry below the cloud tops. Highly elliptical 53-day orbit takes it from inside the radiation belts (perijove ~4200 km above cloud tops) out past Callisto's distance. Confirmed Jupiter has a 'diluted' rocky core (not a sharp boundary), measured the polar cyclone configuration (eight circumpolar storms around each pole), imaged Io's volcanism in unprecedented detail (close-pass 2023-12-30, ~1500 km altitude). Mission extension through September 2025 includes flybys of all four Galilean moons.

events.label: Launch — Atlas V 551
events.description: Cape Canaveral, 2011-08-05. Juno is the first solar-powered spacecraft to reach Jupiter — three massive solar arrays span 20 m tip-to-tip, generating 14 kW at Earth distance but only ~500 W at Jupiter (5.4 AU). The polar orbit was chosen to minimise time inside Jupiter's lethal radiation belts.

events.label: Earth — gravity assist
events.description: Closest approach 559 km on 2013-10-09. The flyby added 7.3 km/s to Juno's heliocentric velocity — the boost needed to reach Jupiter directly (a Hohmann transfer from Earth would have required a far larger launch vehicle than the Atlas V provides).

events.label: Jupiter orbit insertion
events.description: 2016-07-05 UTC (July 4 Pacific time — Independence Day in the US). 35-minute main engine burn slowed Juno from hyperbolic to a highly-elliptical 53-day polar orbit, threading the gap between Jupiter and its main radiation belts. The polar orbit is unique among Jupiter missions — letting Juno map the deep interior + auroras while limiting total radiation dose. Mission extended through 2025.
